DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 101 s. 2022 September 28, 2022 Hon. MA. ROCHELLE V. CAROLINA Municipal Mayor Santa Maria, Laguna Dear Mayor Carolina: This refers to your letter dated May 2, 2022 requesting for guidance and clarification regarding the validity of an order declaring the temporary closure of Marilag Ecological Park issued by the Sangguniang Baranagay of Laurel, Santa Maria, Laguna, through a social media post by its Sangguniang Kabataan Chairperson. You letter was forwarded to the Central Office by DILG-Region IV-Director Ariel Iglesia through a letter dated June IO, 2022 As represented, the management and maintenance of the Eco-Park is shared jointly by the Sangguniang Bayan of Santa Maria and Sangguniang Barangay of Laurel by virtue of Sangguniang Bayan Ordinance No. 004, T-2012. On 29 April 2022, the Sangguniang Bayan of Santa Maria received a report that the Sangguniang Barangay of Laurel through their Sangguniang Kabataan Chairman issued an announcement ordering the temporary closure of Marilag Ecological Park. Apparently, thus measure was done without the consent and approval of the Sangguniang Bayan of Santa Maria and without any prior notice to the latter. Hence, your query. Foremost, it is to be emphasized that this Department is an agency under the executive branch of the government and as such, it is devoid of authority to declare invalid or illegal executive or legislative measures approved by local government officials, nor does it have authority to declare invalid or illegal any acts committed by local government officials which is alleged to be in violation of the Local Government Code (hereinafter referred to as the Code) of any other applicable laws. The same must be threshed out before the proper forum. Notwithstanding, for purposes of academic discussion coupled with our objective to guide the parties concerned, we shall herein discuss the provisions of law which we deem applicable to the subject issue. Section 447 (a) (5) (v) succinctly provides, thus: "The sangguniang bayan, as the legislative body of the municipality, shall enact ordinances, approve resolutions and appropriate funds for the general welfare of the municipality and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code and in the proper exercise of the corporate powers of the municipality as provided for under Section 22 of this Code, and shall: "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.. 8876-34-54

(5) Approve ordinances which shall ensure the efficient and effective delivery of the basic services and facilities as provided for under Section 17 of this Code, and in addition to said services and facilities, shall: (v) Regulate the use of streets, avenues, alleys, sidewalks, bridges, parks and other public places and approve the construction, improvement, repair and maintenance of the same; establish bus and vehicle stops and terminals or regulate the use of the same by privately-owned vehicles which serve the public; regulate garages and the operation of conveyances for hire; designate stands to be occupied by public vehicles when not in use; regulate the putting up of signs, signposts, awnings and awning posts On the streets; provide for the lighting, cleaning and sprinkling of streets and public places. Xxx" As could be clearly deduced from the foregoing, the Code confers upon sangguniang bayan the power to regulate the use of, among others, parks and other public places pursuant to an ordinance. By "regulate" this means the sanggunian bayan may, pursuant to an ordinance, permanently or temporarily close any park falling within its jurisdiction. Along this line, it is worthy to note that barangays, as local government unit, are not precluded to exercise such power pursuant to Section 21 of the Code, thus: "Section 21. Closure and Opening of Roads. - (a) A local government unit may, pursuant to an ordinance, permanently or temporarily close or open any local road, alley, park, or square falling within its jurisdiction: Provided, however, That in case of permanent closure, such ordinance must be approved by at least two-thirds (2/3) of all the members of the sanggunian, and when necessary, an adequate substitute for the public facility that is subject to closure is provided." It is important to note that the foregoing provisions clearly and specifically requires the enactment of an ordinance in the exercise of such power. Premised from the foregoing, it is respectfully opined that the temporary closure of a park without an ordinance duly enacted for that purpose is improper. Even assuming arguendo that the temporary closure of a park was done pursuant to an ordinance, we find it apt for the concerned sangguniang barangay to have discussed the matter with the Sangguniang Bayan before undertaking such action, taking into account that the nature of the management and maintenance of said park. Notwithstanding, we would like to reiterate that the opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations narrated in the letter and our appreciation of the same, and is being issued without prejudice to any contrary opinion, decisions, and orders of more competent authorities or the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY THE AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ICT R.
